name: Frequent Subgraph Mining
problem_statement: Given a collection of graphs, discover unique subgraph patterns appearing in at least a specified fraction of the collection.

normalization: Apply one self-loop and parallel-edge policy consistently to all collection members.
Preserve direction when mining directed patterns.
Use stable categorical values for any labels included in matching.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_support_fraction
problem_inputs.description: Minimum fraction of collection graphs containing at least one pattern occurrence.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_edges
problem_inputs.description: Minimum edges in a returned pattern.

problem_inputs.name: maximum_edges
problem_inputs.description: Maximum edges in a returned pattern.

problem_inputs.name: induced
problem_inputs.description: Use induced containment when measuring support.

required_outputs.name: patterns
required_outputs.description: Canonical pattern graph, support graph count, and support fraction for every frequent pattern.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all qualifying patterns within the size bounds were discovered.

optional_outputs.name: closed_or_maximal_status
optional_outputs.description: Whether a pattern is closed or maximal under support-preserving extension.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate one canonical representative for each isomorphism class whose graph-level support meets the threshold and size bounds.
solution_semantics.exactness: complete=true requires exact exhaustive pattern discovery.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Isomorphic patterns under label_semantics appear once.

validation_rules: Pattern support counts collection members, not raw occurrence multiplicity.
Every reported support meets the threshold.
No two returned patterns are isomorphic under selected label semantics.
edge_cases: An empty collection yields no patterns.
Duplicate copies of a pattern inside one graph contribute only one unit of graph-level support.
A support fraction of one requires presence in every collection member.
